principle_text: When the seller emphasizes the potential illegal or unethical use of the item, avoid making comments that imply misuse or unethical behavior to prevent weakening your negotiation leverage.
When the seller emphasizes the high quality and features of the item, you should combine a legitimate use case with a lower offer to maintain pressure and improve your negotiating position.

When the buyer downplays the product's value by comparing it to a smartphone, avoid implying that the item's incremental value is insufficient for the full price to prevent weakening your negotiating position.
When the seller confirms the item is in excellent condition, avoid asking clarifying questions that do not assert a negotiation position or leverage the information for price discussion.
When the seller confirms included accessories without addressing price adjustments, avoid asking solely about item details to ensure negotiation focus remains on price.
When the seller emphasizes the great condition of the item, you should leverage comparisons to higher-priced new models to negotiate a lower price effectively.
When the seller has already provided a final offer and emphasized the great condition of the item, you should consider offering to pick up the item yourself to negotiate a lower price effectively.

When the seller confirms a value-added feature like warranty transferability, avoid solely focusing on this benefit and ensure to continue negotiating the price to prevent diverting attention from the primary goal of reaching a mutually agreeable price.
When the buyer increases their offer closer to the seller's initial asking price, you should accept the counteroffer to secure a better deal and move the negotiation towards a successful outcome.
When the seller responds to initial buyer interest with questions about usage intent, avoid making vague or non-specific expressions of interest that do not advance price negotiation.
When the seller asks about your intended use or location to assess value or logistics, avoid giving vague or incomplete responses that miss opportunities to establish negotiation leverage.

When the seller responds to a low offer with a moderate price reduction and added value like free shipping, you should make a significantly lower counteroffer to pressure the seller into negotiating downward.
When the seller makes a clear counteroffer with a specific price and shipping terms, avoid immediately accepting without attempting to negotiate further to secure a better deal.
When the seller maintains a firm counteroffer above your initial price, you should justify your lower offer by highlighting specific item drawbacks to create leverage for negotiation.
When the seller provides a firm counteroffer correcting inaccurate buyer claims, you should use accurate market information to adjust your offer and maintain credibility in price negotiations.
When the seller makes a final price offer, you should propose adding value through extras or bonuses to improve the deal without demanding further price reductions.
When the seller has made a final offer and agreed to add value without lowering price, you should accept the deal to secure the agreed terms and avoid prolonging negotiation unnecessarily.
When the seller acknowledges the item is somewhat older but still functional, you should use the item's age as leverage to justify negotiating a lower price.

When the seller emphasizes recent improvements or repairs that enhance the item's condition, avoid asking questions that highlight potential flaws without a strategy to leverage them for a price reduction.

When the seller counters with a midpoint price between their initial offer and your target, you should initiate negotiation by clearly stating your desired lower price to create leverage and prompt concessions.
When the seller makes a counteroffer below their initial price, avoid immediately accepting without attempting further negotiation to maintain leverage and potentially achieve a better deal.
When the seller shows willingness to negotiate price, you should propose a lower offer and add incentives like immediate payment or pickup to encourage a better counteroffer.
When the seller makes a reasonable counteroffer that narrows the price gap, you should accept it to secure a better deal and close the negotiation efficiently.
When the seller responds by emphasizing product features without addressing price, avoid using questions about product use that do not directly relate to negotiating a better price.
When the seller reaffirms a high initial price without engaging the buyer's lower offer, avoid weakening your position by lowering your offer or using unverifiable emotional appeals.
When the seller responds to a buyer's increased offer by lowering their counteroffer, you should make a reasonable concession to encourage further movement toward agreement.

When the seller clarifies the absence of an accessory but highlights included original packaging, avoid focusing solely on accessory absence without linking it to price negotiation or value adjustment.
When the seller states a firm initial price and confirms item availability, you should directly propose your target price to potentially secure an immediate agreement.
When the seller has already agreed to a price, avoid pushing for a lower price immediately afterward as it can weaken your negotiation position and reduce the likelihood of further concessions.
When the seller reveals the item is brand new but not suitable for their needs, you should justify your target price by framing it as a reasonable alternative for a specific user or purpose.
When the seller has already agreed to your target price, avoid shifting the negotiation focus prematurely to logistical details that do not affect the price.
When the seller has already accepted your target price and agreed on terms, avoid introducing new negotiation points that do not advance the deal or improve your position.
When the seller responds with a basic product description without engaging on price, avoid vague or non-specific requests that do not prompt negotiation or price discussion.
When the seller clearly indicates that a buyer's offer is too low, avoid making aggressive price reductions that undermine your leverage and stall productive negotiation.
When the seller clearly states a firm final price with limited room for negotiation, avoid making criticisms that may provoke a defensive response and reduce your leverage.
When the seller states a firm final price and refuses further negotiation, avoid immediately accepting the offer without attempting to leverage additional value or negotiate terms.
When the seller emphasizes that a missing feature does not affect the item's functionality, avoid focusing on that feature as a bargaining point since it may strengthen the seller's position.
When the seller conditionally accepts your target price, you should confirm your offer firmly to anchor the negotiation and secure favorable terms.
When the seller agrees to a lower price contingent on a specific condition, you should accept the condition promptly to secure the favorable price and finalize the deal efficiently.
When the seller responds to a higher buyer offer by introducing urgency or other buyers instead of addressing the price, avoid conceding too quickly without securing a better price agreement.
When the seller indicates they have other interested buyers and asks about pickup timing, avoid emphasizing urgency or quick pickup that can give the seller leverage to increase the price.
When the seller confirms product features or warranties without changing price terms, avoid asking purely informational questions that do not advance your negotiation position.
When the seller expresses willingness to negotiate and invites an offer, you should confidently state your target price clearly to potentially secure an immediate agreement.
When the seller has already agreed to your target price, avoid unnecessary additional responses that do not advance the negotiation or improve your position.
When the seller is clarifying item details or asking for pricing information, avoid repeating item descriptions without introducing a price offer or negotiation tactic.
When the seller maintains a firm initial price, avoid conceding to or repeating that price without a stronger counteroffer, as it weakens your negotiation leverage.
When the seller proposes an ambiguous swap without clear terms, avoid agreeing without clarification to prevent losing leverage and facing unexpected price escalations.
When the seller proposes a high-value offer or swap that exceeds your budget, you should clearly state your maximum price limit and willingness to walk away to create negotiation leverage.
When the seller clearly states a firm minimum price, you should consider accepting that counteroffer if it aligns closely with your budget to reach a timely agreement.
When the seller maintains a firm initial price but shows willingness to negotiate, you should present a clear, firm offer close to your target price to encourage the seller to lower their price.
When the seller makes a reasonable counteroffer close to your initial price, avoid immediately accepting without attempting further negotiation to secure a better deal.
When the seller responds neutrally and asks for a specific proposal, avoid vague or non-committal negotiation inquiries that fail to establish clear leverage or terms.

When the seller rejects a low price but offers to include a trade-in item to supplement the offer, you should propose your target price clearly to anchor the negotiation and open pathways for alternative deals.
When the seller proposes a trade-in item to supplement a lower cash offer, you should confirm possession of the item to strengthen your bargaining position and encourage further negotiation.
When the seller expresses skepticism about the value of a trade item, you should reveal specific details about that item to prompt the seller to adjust their price offer.
When the seller proposes a price with conditional trade-ins, you should offer alternative combinations of cash and trade items to create pressure and increase chances of a favorable price concession.
When the seller shares positive features to reinforce the item's value, avoid using purely rapport-building questions that do not directly address price or terms.
When the seller has emphasized the product's new condition and advanced technology, you should proactively propose a lower price than your initial offer to create leverage and anchor the negotiation.
